messages:
emily (oncall): paging — p99 latency spike observed on streaming/generate and streaming/chat across us-west-2 and eu-west-1. Alerts: p99_stream_latency > 2.5s, streaming_stalls_inc > 50/min. customers: two high-throughput tenants show errors. Notified on-call.

raj (sre): ack. I'm looking at the dashboard now. kv_cache_evictions_total spiked ~00:07 UTC, and kv_cache_hit_ratio dropped from 92% -> 61%. Eviction rate correlates with stalls.

maria (ml-infra): grabbing KV cache shard metrics. I'm seeing fragmentation on shard-7: active_keys oscillating and many small segments causing GC-like sweeps. Prefill job backlog is high (prefill_queue_len ~ 1200) while decode throughput dropped.

emily (oncall): ops-bot, please page the SRE rotation and create an incident ticket.

ops-bot: :rotating_light: Incident created: INC-2026-3141 — Latency spike (p99) affecting streaming endpoints. Severity: P1. Pager notified.

raj (sre): quick mitigation suggestions: 1) throttle prefill worker concurrency to reduce prefill vs decode imbalance, 2) temporarily increase KV cache capacity for affected pool, 3) force compaction on fragmented shards, 4) switch affected routes to fallback model variant with smaller KV footprint.

maria (ml-infra): agree. Prefill workers are saturating IO; prefill->cache writes are causing eviction pressure because decode threads are CPU-bound and lagging. We can scale down prefill concurrency with one config flip: 

```
POST /admin/prefill/config
{
  "concurrency": 6  // from 20
}
```

That should reduce writes to cache for 30s-2min before queue drains.

tom (platform): we can bump the kv cache quota for the dedicated pool for 10m. Running:

```
kubectl -n infra exec config-manager -- curl -XPOST "http://localhost:8080/cache/resize" -d '{"pool":"streaming-prod","size_gb":160}'
```

This will increase capacity and reduce eviction churn. Doing it now.

maria (ml-infra): while tom does that, I'm going to trigger compaction on shard-7 and shard-3. compaction reduces fragmentation; should reduce tail decode latency. Command:

```
./kvctl compact --shard 7 --shard 3 --force
```

I expect compaction to take ~45s per shard.

luis (product): which customers are impacted? Any paying enterprise SLAs at risk?

emily (oncall): initial customer impact list: tenant:openai-proxy (high qps), tenant:medscribe (healthcare). Both have low-latency SLAs; product alerted account teams. Currently errors are streaming stalls (retries) but non-streaming endpoints mostly OK.

raj (sre): update: tom confirmed cache resize accepted. kv_cache_capacity increased from 120GB -> 160GB for streaming-prod. Eviction rate dropped ~40% within 20s. p99 streaming latency improved from ~3.4s -> ~1.6s but p95 still elevated.

maria (ml-infra): compaction finished for shard-7, shard-3 still running. Fragmentation metric fragment_ratio went from 0.54 -> 0.18 on shard-7. decode_worker_latency p99 dropped significantly for shard-7 requests.

emily (oncall): rolling handoff in 10m — raj, can you lead the next 30m and I’ll pass to afternoon on-call after that? Put short notes in the incident ticket.

raj (sre): taking lead. Plan: keep prefill concurrency reduced for 15m, monitor prefill_queue_len and decode throughput. If p99 remains >2s, consider routing small requests to fallback model variant (routed by policy) to reduce KV pressure.

maria (ml-infra): note: fallback model has ~40% smaller KV footprint, but slightly higher decode CPU cost. For short-term it's preferable.

tom (platform): routing change can be applied via policy: 

```
POST /policy/route
{
  "selector":"streaming-prod",
  "fallback_model":"redwood-small-v2",
  "percentage":100
}
```

I suggest waiting 10m to see compaction effects before flipping.

raj (sre): visible improvement so far. p99 -> 1.3s across us-west-2 after compactions and cache bump. However we still see occasional streaming stalls tied to a small subset of long-context requests that thrash the KV cache (context > 12k tokens). I'm going to add a short-term guard: throttle requests with context > 12k tokens to reduce tail pressure.

emily (oncall): how many requests are long-context? impact on customers?

maria (ml-infra): <0.2% of requests but they account for ~18% of kv cache evictions. Targeted throttling should reduce eviction churn a lot.

luis (product): can we notify impacted customers proactively? medscribe is in HC; need to ensure they know about mitigation.

emily (oncall): I'm drafting an outbound note: "We're investigating increased streaming latency; we've applied mitigations (cache resize and compaction) and are throttling extremely long-context requests. We're monitoring and will update."

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-3141 updated: severity remains P1. Postmortem owner assigned: raj. Estimated next update in 15m.

raj (sre): plan for next hour: 1) monitor p95/p99, 2) track kv_cache_evictions_total and fragment_ratio, 3) keep prefill concurrency low until prefill backlog < 100, 4) schedule a controlled rollout of fallback model if p99 regresses. Also collect a sample of long-context request traces for postmortem.

emily (oncall): handing off to raj now. I’ll add my notes to ticket and notify account teams. If anything regresses, page me on-call.

raj (sre): acknowledged, taking over. Thanks emily.

maria (ml-infra): leaving compaction and metrics alarms on; I'll stick around for the next update.

tom (platform): I'll follow up with a hotfix to make the prefill concurrency a circuit-breaker rather than manual flip — file: PLATFORM-2987.

emily (oncall): closing short-term loop: immediate mitigations helped but root cause still looks like cache fragmentation + prefill/decode imbalance. Postmortem should include: upgrade to smarter prefill backpressure, compaction scheduling, and routing policy for long-context. Thanks team :thumbsup:

ops-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident action items logged to INC-2026-3141. Postmortem assigned to @raj. Follow-up meeting scheduled 2026-03-15 16:00 UTC.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-3141 severity downgraded to P2 — system stabilized. Further tracking in ticket.

raj (sre): leaving a final note in thread: samples saved (/var/incident/INC-2026-3141/traces.tar.gz). Will produce a postmortem with timeline + remediation in 48h.

emily (oncall): thanks everyone. Handed off.
